source.title_on_document: Agency Configurations in Generative AI Ideation: How Textual and Visual Idea Concretizations Shape Idea Creativity and Ideator Effort

supplement.where: Online appendix at https://doi.org/10.1287/isre.2024.0952 (PDF p. 2, 'Supplemental Material')
supplement.holds: Online Appendix A (interaction flows, initial-idea examples), B (prompts), C (scale items), D (descriptives and scale validation), E1 (bootstrapping at low idea maturity), E2 (separate Prolific sample using ChatGPT freely), E3 (alternative operationalizations). Arm-level descriptives, per-arm sample sizes, separate novelty and usefulness results, and the E2 sample's details are not in the main text.

paper_design_summary: 276 U.S. Prolific participants were randomly assigned in a three-cell between-subjects online experiment to refine an idea for improving a crowded train with AI-generated textual concretizations (GPT-3.5 usage scenarios), AI-generated visual concretizations (DALL-E 3 images), or no AI (instructions to imagine the idea in a usage context). Each idea iteration (428 refinements) was scored for creativity as the average of an embedding-based novelty score and a GPT-4o-judged usefulness score; ideator effort was measured from keystrokes and time. A separate Prolific sample that used ChatGPT freely is reported only in the online appendix.

studies.label: Main online experiment (train-improvement idea refinement with textual vs visual AI concretizations vs no AI)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Condition: AI-generated textual concretization, AI-generated visual concretization, or no-concretization control
assignment.quote: Moreover, although we randomly assigned ideators to experimental groups, ideators' preferences or their prior GenAI experiences might have influenced our results.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 13 (journal p. 12), Section 6.3; design described as 'a three-cell, betweensubjects online experiment' at PDF p. 8 (journal p. 7), Section 4.1

arms.name: Textual concretization
arms.description: After describing an initial idea, participant receives a GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613) textual usage scenario of the idea and is encouraged to refine the idea; can iterate until satisfied.

arms.name: Visual concretization
arms.description: Same process, but GPT turns the idea into a prompt for DALL-E 3 and the participant sees the generated image.

arms.name: Control (no concretization)
arms.description: Same process, but instead of a concretization the participant receives instructions to imagine the idea and its outcomes in a usage context.

participants.exclusions: Not stated. The paper says 276 participants were recruited and contributed 428 idea refinements; the regressions use N = 428 refinements (endnote 5). Per-arm counts and any exclusions are not given in the main text. 276 is recorded as analyzed because it is the count of people who contributed the analyzed refinements; the paper does not label it as a count at assignment.
participants.who: U.S.-based Prolific participants; mean age 41.3, 43.8% female, 77.8% with at least a bachelor's degree, 74.2% working full or part time
participants.quote: We recruited 276 U.S.-based participants through Prolific (mean age = 41.3 years old, 43.8% female, 77.8% with at least a bachelor's degree, and 74.2% working full or part time) who contributed a total of 428 idea refinements.

ai_tool.name_model: gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 (textual concretizations; also writes the DALL-E prompt) and DALL-E 3 (visual concretizations)
ai_tool.how_used: Participant writes an initial idea; the AI renders that idea as a textual usage scenario or as an image (visual arm uses image generation); participant then refines the textual idea description and may iterate. AI elaborates the participant's own idea rather than supplying new ideas; no free chat.

task.description: Answer 'What improvements could be made to a crowded train to enhance the experience from boarding to alighting?' (mirrors a real open-innovation challenge); US$2 pay, US$4 bonus for the 10 best ideas.

outcomes.name: Idea creativity (average of novelty and usefulness), z-standardized at the iteration level
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Novelty: all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings, three-nearest-neighbor similarity among ideas at the same refinement iteration (Just et al. 2024). Usefulness: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 as judge of feasibility, elaboration, and inclusivity, each iteration scored three times and averaged. Creativity = mean of novelty and usefulness. Validation against 88 Prolific raters on 158 ideas: Pearson r = 0.27 (endnote 3). Separate novelty and usefulness results are not reported in the main text; robustness to alternative operationalizations is in Online Appendix E3.

contrasts.reported: Model (1a): Textual Concretization 0.29** (0.11); Model (1b) with controls 0.23* (0.10); Model (1c) 0.20* (0.08) with Textual Concretization x Idea Maturity 0.24** (0.09). N = 428; OLS, clustered robust SEs. Text: 'This represents an improvement in creativity of 18%' (endnote 6: 0.29 SD; 60th vs 51st percentile).
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10 (journal p. 9), Table 2 and Section 5; endnote 6 on PDF p. 14 (journal p. 13)

contrasts.reported: Model (1a): Visual Concretization 0.13 (0.10); Model (1b) 0.17† (0.10) [† p <= 0.10]; Model (1c) 0.14 (0.10). N = 428.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10 (journal p. 9), Table 2; PDF p. 11 (journal p. 10), Section 5

contrasts.reported: 'Textual concretizations produced a 30% increase in idea creativity compared with the control condition, which is a statistically significant difference.' No coefficient, SE, or p-value printed (backward difference coding gives only textual vs visual and visual vs control).

outcomes.name: Ideator effort (log of mean of scaled keystrokes and time spent)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Process measure, not a creativity score: number of keystrokes (including deletions and edits) and time between first and last keystroke, scaled, averaged, and log-transformed. Recorded for completeness; it answers none of the three questions.

contrasts.reported: Model (2a): Textual Concretization 0.24** (0.08); Model (2b) 0.17** (0.06); Model (2c) 0.16*** (0.04), Textual x Idea Maturity 0.23** (0.08). '30% more effort than visual concretization.'
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10 (journal p. 9), Table 2; PDF p. 11 (journal p. 10), Section 5

contrasts.reported: Model (2a): Visual Concretization -0.26*** (0.07); Model (2b) -0.16*** (0.05); Model (2c) -0.16*** (0.04). 'reduced ideator effort by 24% relative to the control group'.

assignment.quote: Second, to assess ecological validity, we asked a separate Prolific sample to complete the same ideation task while freely using ChatGPT (see Online Appendix E2).

arms.name: Unguided ChatGPT
arms.description: Separate Prolific sample, same ideation task, free ChatGPT use

participants.exclusions: Not stated in the main text; details in Online Appendix E2, which is not in this PDF.
participants.quote: The ideas produced with unguided ChatGPT use were less creative than those generated with our textual and visual concretizations.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT (version not stated in main text)
ai_tool.how_used: Free use of ChatGPT while completing the same ideation task.

task.description: Same crowded-train improvement task as S1

outcomes.name: Idea creativity (same automated score as S1)
outcomes.question: with_ai

company_involvement.description: No company involvement stated. Uses OpenAI models (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, DALL-E 3, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 as judge). Funding: Swiss National Science Foundation [Grant 248164].
company_involvement.locator: PDF p. 2, Funding; PDF p. 8, Section 4.1

eligibility.reason: S1 randomly assigned individuals (stated only in the limitations, PDF p. 13) to two generative-AI arms and a no-AI control in a between-subjects online experiment; 276 people contributed the analyzed refinements, well above 50 even though per-arm counts are not given; creativity is an automated score (embedding novelty plus LLM-judged usefulness) on each idea iteration. Caveats: analysis unit is the idea iteration (N = 428) with clustered robust SEs whose cluster level is not stated explicitly; the textual vs control contrast has no printed statistic.

one_line_finding: AI textual concretizations raised automated idea creativity relative to visual concretizations by 0.29 SD (SE 0.11, p <= 0.01, N = 428 refinements from 276 people; Table 2, PDF p. 10), visual vs no-AI control was 0.13 (0.10), and textual vs control is described as a significant 30% increase without a printed statistic.
open_questions: Per-arm participant counts and any exclusions are not in the main text; Online Appendix D may hold them.
Clustered robust standard errors: the text implies ideator-level clustering ('to capture differences at the ideator level') but does not name the cluster variable.
The 428 'idea refinements' appear to include control-arm iterations and possibly initial ideas; the main text does not say whether each participant's initial idea is among the 428.
No coefficient is printed for textual concretization vs control; would need Online Appendix or posted data.
Role coding: the AI elaborates the participant's own idea into a scenario or image; 'refinement' chosen, though the visual arm is image generation.
notes: Randomization is stated only in the limitations section. Creativity outcome is z-standardized at the iteration level; effort is log-scaled. Control arm received imagination instructions, not AI, so arm-vs-control contrasts are ai_vs_bau. Outcomes measured during the AI-supported session; no after_ai or diversity outcome. Robustness: bootstrap at low maturity (Appendix E1) finds visual concretizations raise creativity for ideas more than 1 SD below mean maturity.
